title: Pursue fflas-like GF(251) GEMM performance
description:
Follow-up research/optimization work for the GF(251) cells amended to aspirational during `cc5de315` closure.

## Background

Story `cc5de315` closed the current GF(p) parity contract with a user-approved amendment: GF(251) remains below the 1.5x-of-fflas hard threshold because fflas-ffpack routes GF(251) through an OpenBLAS-backed float-modular cascade, while gf2-core currently uses a pure AVX2 hand-written packed-byte kernel. The amendment does not mean the gap is uninteresting; it means it is non-blocking for the SOTA closure story.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A design or prototype identifies the highest-leverage route toward fflas-like GF(251) performance, including whether the likely path is Goto-style cache blocking, an f32/BLAS-like cascade, VNNI/AVX-512 routing, or an explicit out-of-scope external BLAS dependency.
- [hard] The work includes reproducible GF(251) benchmark evidence at n in {256, 1024} using the same pinned/reference methodology as `cc5de315`.
- [hard] If production code changes are made, they preserve correctness for GF(7), GF(31), GF(251), Mersenne31, and Fp<65537> and do not regress existing GF(p) cells by more than 5% under same-session measurement.
- [hard] If the conclusion is that fflas-like parity requires a larger architectural or dependency change, the recommendation is recorded as a design/evidence document and wired to the appropriate future epic rather than blocking `cc5de315`.
